To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) allele dropout probability decreases for each PCR cycle increase from 30 to about 33 PCR cycles, and (ii) allele dropouts are mainly affected by DNA quantity and not by the number of PCR and/or CE cycles
the number of PCR amplification cycles can be extended from 30 to a maximum of 33 without increasing the risk for allele dropouts.
allele dropout risk can be decreased by increasing the number of amplification cycles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the detection limits of STR analysis and with the understanding of allele dropouts and allele imbalance.
the development of models to assess the impact of DNA amount, PCR and CE settings on the quality of EPGs.
optimisation of the analysis of low-template DNA samples and the understanding of the impact of different PCR cycle numbers and CE settings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
32 PCR cycles with 5, 8, 10, or 15 CE injection seconds is optimal for LT DNA analysis.
allele dropout probabilities decrease with increased number of PCR cycles, whereas the heterozygote balances and stutters are not directly affected by this.
the use of enhanced PCR and CE settings is beneficial for low-template DNA analysis, but the benefits are limited and depend on the DNA quantity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
32 PCR cycles with 5-10 CE injection seconds is a good compromise between allele dropout probability and CE saturation, and that 32 PCR cycle amplification is sufficient for most samples.
30 cycles is too few, 33 cycles too many, and 32 cycles are optimal for STR analysis.
32 PCR cycles with 30 s CE injection is the optimal setting for the STR analysis kit PowerPex ESX 16 and 5-10 s CE injection can be used for 33 and 34 cycles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
allele dropout probability is affected by DNA quantity and PCR cycle number.
allele dropout probabilities are not directly affected by the number of PCR amplification cycles.
32 PCR cycles with 5-10 CE injection seconds is a good choice for STR analysis of LT DNA.
